page: Microsoft Azure D64pds_v6 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the Dpdsv6 family, powered by an ARM-based Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz with no hyperthreading. The memory configuration consists of 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, featuring a 3780 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10%. Memory subsystem performance is also highly rated, with large-block read and write memory bandwidth scoring in the top 10%. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core results falling in the middle 50% range.

Given its ARM architecture, the D64pds_v6 offers high resource density and power efficiency, translating to a cost-effective profile for multi-threaded workloads compared to traditional x86 architectures. The combination of 64 dedicated cores, high memory bandwidth, and a large local NVMe SSD makes it highly suitable for database operations, software compilation, and static web serving. It is also well-suited for multi-threaded data processing, while being less optimal for workloads heavily reliant on single-core clock speed or specialized x86 instruction sets like AVX.

Conversely, single-core performance remains in the average tier. This hardware profile provides a cost-effective, high-density solution for multi-threaded workloads.
